claims.statement: The native Android host lives in packages/android-host (@pictelio/android-host) and is explicitly not a client; the only client is @pictelio/app-lynx (packages/app-lynx). The former packages/app WebView client and its Capacitor/three-flavor Android tree were deleted, and the Java host was migrated verbatim to packages/android-host/android (ADR-0203).

The Android project is a single-engine Gradle module with no product flavors: the former lynx flavor's src/lynx/java is promoted as an additional main source directory, CLIENT_KINDS is collapsed to {"lynx"}, and the manifest resolves the launcher to .LynxActivity and the Application to .PictelioAppLynx via placeholders.

The host builds with minSdk 28, compileSdk/targetSdk 36, buildTools 36.1.0, and Java 21; build.gradle's checked-in values are versionCode 60800 / versionName 6.8.0, and sync-android-version.mjs rewrites both from packages/app-lynx/package.json using major×10000 + minor×100 + patch.

Pixiv OAuth credentials and endpoint config are generated into io.pictelio.app.config.OAuthConfig by sync-credentials.mjs reading ../app-lynx/credentials.json5; Gradle compilation depends on this gitignored generated class, so gradlew entry points must run sync:credentials first.

The dual-engine availability fallback of ADR-0153/ADR-0164 is removed: with the WebView client deleted there is no fallback target, and LynxActivity.onFatal converges init failure, bundle load failure, fatal render error, and the 10s timeout into a single exit-only error page with no failure memory and no automatic engine switch.

LynxRuntimeInitializer is the idempotent runtime init point (InitGate latches only on success, so a failed init stays retryable) shared by PictelioAppLynx.onCreate and LynxActivity.onCreate; in order it registers LynxHttpService, LynxLogService and PictelioImageService as services, calls LynxEnv.init, globally registers 12 LynxModules (PictelioSecureStorage, PictelioApp, PictelioAuth, PictelioApi, PictelioPrefs, PictelioGallery, PictelioDownloader, PictelioShare, NetDiag, PictelioWebDav, PictelioClipboard, PictelioNotification), enables LynxDebug for debug builds, and exposes isAvailable as a CLIENT_KINDS + init-no-throw + native-library-loaded probe.

LynxActivity is the sole launcher Activity (plain AppCompatActivity, no Capacitor), installs SplashScreen before super.onCreate and holds the splash via bundleLoaded, serves main.lynx.bundle through PictelioTemplateProvider with XElement behaviors, registers an 8-module per-view set on the LynxViewBuilder (PictelioSecureStorage, PictelioApp, PictelioAuth, PictelioApi, PictelioTranslate, PictelioTranslateCache, PictelioPrefs, NetDiag — only the two translation modules are per-view-only, the rest duplicate the global registration where the global LynxEnv registration wins), and forwards lifecycle events to the LynxView.

PictelioApiModule.request forwards Pixiv API calls with the contract cb(status, data, rotatedRefreshToken) and keeps the access token inside Java; it resolves an Accept-Language header from settings_language (en -> en, otherwise zh-CN) and delegates to PixivApiCore.executeRequest for Bearer/Referer/UA injection plus 401-refresh-and-retry-once.

PixivApiCore holds accessToken/refreshToken as static volatile Java-heap fields (never exposed to JS), performs a synchronized 401 refresh with an isRefreshing guard and reference-identity token comparison, retries once, and performs the OAuth refresh-token exchange using MD5 X-Client-Time/Hash signing over a shared tuned OkHttpClient singleton.

PictelioAuthModule.loginWithRefreshToken writes the access token only into PixivApiCore.accessToken and returns userInfoJson plus a possibly-rotated refresh token to JS; setAccessToken is the one-way JS->Java push and clearTokens nulls both heap fields on logout.

SecureStorageCompat is a byte-compatible reimplementation of @aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage 8.x (ADR-0050): AES/GCM/NoPadding in AndroidKeyStore with one key per capacitor-storage_<key> alias, ciphertext stored in WSSecureStorageSharedPreferences as Base64(ciphertext)+U+0010+Base64(iv).

Android backup excludes the Keystore ciphertext file WSSecureStorageSharedPreferences.xml and the historical plaintext residue PictelioPrefs.xml from both cloud backup and device transfer via data_extraction_rules.xml (API 31+) and backup_rules.xml, wired by the manifest's allowBackup/dataExtractionRules/fullBackupContent attributes.

WebDavClient implements the minimal WebDAV subset (MKCOL with 409-as-success, PUT, GET, PROPFIND Depth 0/1, DELETE) over OkHttp Basic auth, classifies failures into a Kind enum, performs write-then-verify uploads (PUT then PROPFIND getcontentlength, GET byte-compare fallback, up to 3 retries), and prunes to the last 10 timestamp-named backups.

BackupCrypto implements the v1 backup envelope PICTELIO-ENC1 magic (13B) + salt (16B) + iv (12B) + AES-256-GCM ciphertext, with the key derived by PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600k iterations from the user password, so passwords never enter the backup file.

PictelioWebDavModule is the thin Lynx bridge over WebDavClient/BackupCrypto (ensureDir/upload/uploadWithVerify/download/list/stat/delete/prune/encrypt/decrypt/isEncrypted), crossing bytes as base64 and always invoking cb(code, payload) with a JSON error object on failure.

The download/export bridge routes through PictelioDownloaderModule (start/pollProgress/cancel/deleteFile) into the shared PictelioDownloader executor, which fetches bytes via PixivImageLoader.loadFileWithProgress and lands them via GallerySaver: MediaStore (Pictures/Pictelio, IS_PENDING) on API 29+, app-specific external dir plus MediaScanner on API 28, with Downloads/Pictelio for non-image products.

NovelExporter implements 9 output formats (txt/html/md/rtf/json/fb2 plus epub/docx via ZipOutputStream and pdf via PdfDocument+StaticLayout), and UgoiraExporter implements zip/tar/apng while delegating gif/webp/mp4 to dedicated encoders, with all encoding in Java so bytes never enter the JS heap.

PixivImageLoader is the single image-download source of truth (URL rewrite, Referer/UA injection, disk cache, per-URL lock); ImageHostConfig.resolve picks the download source per request with the cache key fixed to the official URL; and PictelioImageService is the custom ILynxImageService that delegates to PixivImageLoader, registers image behaviors, and serves static Bitmaps with a zero-copy cached delivery.

LynxActivity owns the native system-UI contract: EdgeToEdge base, content size = LynxView bounds minus visible system-bar insets (physical px, converted to logical px on the JS side), a pull-first pictelioInsets event plus getSafeAreaInsets, a fullscreen toggle keyed on settings_fullscreen_mode (only "true" is truthy) whose hide/show also writes back the statusBarHidden latch so status-bar appearance is re-issued on exit-fullscreen, and a three-state settings_dark_mode (light/dark/system) driving status-bar icon appearance and the API 31+ splash theme — while the pictelioDarkMode event itself reports the system uiMode.

Release ProGuard/R8 rules keep Lynx JNI lookups (LynxBaseTrace/LynxLog), PictelioImageService, Lynx-generated $$PropsSetter/$$PropsHolder constructors plus members, and Room-generated WorkDatabase_Impl constructors, and add dontwarn for deliberately-absent Fresco/Gson/Markdown classes.

PictelioTranslateModule exposes seven @LynxMethods over the OpenAI Responses API (setApiKey / getEndpoint / clearEndpoint / translateStream / translatePoll / probeEndpoint / abortStream) with the API key stored through SecureStorageCompat and never returned to JS, delivering SSE frames primarily by publishing seq-stamped frames on the pictelioTranslateFrame global event with translatePoll as a pull fallback; PictelioTranslateCacheModule is a filesystem LRU cache (default 10 MB / 200 entries) under cacheDir/pictelio_translate_cache with a manifest.json index and atomic temp+rename writes.

PictelioNotificationModule is the delivery-probe bridge registered globally as PictelioNotification with exactly two @LynxMethods — areNotificationsEnabled (reflects the real system switch and degrades to "not granted" with a warning instead of throwing) and postSummary (creates the pictelio_delivery_probe channel via createNotificationChannel, then posts one aggregated notification under a fixed notification id so rounds overwrite instead of stack). It never requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS and never writes counters, and assembles the wording host-side from a locale string while stating only the count; the manifest declares android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS so a runtime grant can succeed.

Notification taps are routed through NotificationTapActivity, a NoDisplay trampoline declared exported=false with excludeFromRecents/noHistory and targeted by PendingIntent.getActivity: it is the one place that runs at tap time inside the app process and is exempt from the Android 10+ background-Activity-launch restriction, and it copies the "notifications" target plus the per-delivery clickId onto a LynxActivity intent. LynxActivity.dispatchNotificationTarget then persists the pending clickId with commit() and broadcasts pictelioNotificationTarget four times at fixed 1.5 / 3 / 4.5 / 6 s delays, deduped JS-side by clickId; warm taps require onNewIntent to call setIntent(intent), without which the click extras are dropped silently.

LynxActivity sends the pictelioAppForeground global event in onResume and pictelioAppBackground in onPause via sendGlobalEvent, with no debounce; these are the only JS-visible foreground/background channel, because LynxView.onEnterForeground() does not become a JS event and Lynx exposes no window-focus event.

The translation frame delivery path snapshots the seq-stamped frame buffers and pushes them through the global event bus without draining them, so frames survive a window in which no JS listener exists and translatePoll's terminal handshake performs the cleanup; abortStream records the streamId in a USER_ABORTED set before cancelling the OkHttp call, because Call.isCanceled() cannot distinguish a user abort from a client-side timeout and conflating them left the JS promise permanently unsettled with the UI stuck mid-translation.

Preference values returned by PictelioPrefsModule cross the Lynx bridge JSON-quoted, so JS must apply its unquoteNativeString helper before JSON.parse (the on-device XML layer's " escaping is a separate layer); a key that does not exist is returned as an empty string rather than null.
